transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Microwaves store lethal voltages in their capacitors even when unplugged, and working inside them is strictly for qualified engineers. This is almost always a fault in the high-voltage heating circuit (which includes parts like the magnetron, HV diode, capacitor, or inverter board depending on your model), though it can sometimes be caused by selecting the wrong power level. 1. Please confirm you were using a normal cooking mode (e.g. 100% power) and not 'Defrost' or a low setting.
2. Try heating a cup of water on full power for one minute. Is the water still cold? Once you've checked that, let me know the result and I'll guide you through the next safe steps.
